overall_result.mathematical_status: valid modulo the standard approximation theorems and explicit representative convention below
overall_result.summary: Both conclusions follow with strict slack, including a=b and C=0. The noise theorem must reuse the single witness constructed at half tolerance. Almost-everywhere range hypotheses must not be strengthened to pointwise hypotheses.

conventions.interval: I=[a,b], interpreted as restriction of Lebesgue measure to the closed set I.
conventions.integral: Integrals are set-restricted Lebesgue integrals, not oriented interval integrals.
conventions.exceptional_values: No restriction on f off I or on the null exceptional subset of I.
conventions.square_root: Classically, define the noise integrand using a nonnegative a.e. representative of f, or extend real sqrt to negative inputs (for example by sqrt(max(x,0))). These choices agree a.e. and give the same integral. The displayed expression is otherwise not pointwise defined where f<0 on the exceptional null set.
conventions.globally_smooth: g has derivatives of every finite order on all of R. Its strict positivity and upper bound are asserted only on I.

common_premises.assertion: 0<=f(t)<=C for almost every t under Lebesgue measure restricted to I.
Lebesgue measure of I is b-a and finite, including measure zero when a=b.
Continuous functions are L1-dense on a finite compact real interval; the approximant may be taken globally continuous, via an ambient theorem or continuous extension.
A continuous real function can be approximated by a globally C-infinity function uniformly on a compact interval, with any prescribed positive tolerance.
Measurable functions dominated a.e. in norm by an integrable function are integrable; integral monotonicity and triangle inequality apply to the integrable quantities.
Square root on nonnegative real numbers is monotone and satisfies (sqrt x)^2=x, including x=0.
The noise integrand has a measurable real-valued definition on exceptional points, or denotes an a.e.-defined function.

theorem_contracts.quantifier_structure: For every admissible a,b,C,epsilon,f there exists one g:R->R.
For every admissible a,b,C,epsilon,f there exists one and the same g:R->R satisfying all conclusions.
theorem_contracts.witness: The T1 witness with tolerance epsilon/2; no second independent witness.

nodes.claim: Set I=[a,b], L=b-a. L>=0, measure(I)=L, and measure(I)<infinity.
|f(t)|<=C a.e. on I, by the stated nonnegative bounded range. Measurability restricts from R to I.
f is integrable on I by domination by constant C on a finite-measure set.
Choose continuous q on R with Integral_I |f-q|<=epsilon/2. A theorem giving strict error <epsilon/2 suffices. Global boundedness of q is unnecessary; continuity on I implies boundedness there.
Define u(t)=max(0,min(C,q(t))). The function u is globally continuous and pointwise 0<=u<=C.
Where f(t) lies in [0,C], |u(t)-f(t)|<=|q(t)-f(t)|. Thus Integral_I |u-f|<=epsilon/2. Integrability follows from f integrable and u bounded/continuous.
delta=epsilon/(4*(L+1)); L+1>0 and delta>0.
The closed one-neighborhood of I, equivalently [a-1,b+1], is compact. Restriction of the continuous u to it is uniformly continuous.
Choose globally smooth v with |v(t)-u(t)|<=delta/2 on I, using positive tolerance and a compact-neighborhood smoothing theorem.
2*delta=epsilon/(2*(L+1))<=epsilon/2<=epsilon; in particular 3*delta/2<=epsilon.
Define g=v+delta, globally smooth as a smooth function plus a constant.
For t in I, delta/2<=g(t)<=C+3*delta/2. Consequently 0<g(t)<=C+epsilon.
For t in I, |g(t)-u(t)|<=|v(t)-u(t)|+delta<=3*delta/2<=2*delta.
g,u,v and their differences are integrable on I by continuity and finite compactness. g-f and u-f and their absolute values are integrable using N03.
Integral_I |g-u|<=2*delta*L.
2*delta*L=epsilon*L/(2*(L+1))<epsilon/2 because L<L+1 and epsilon>0, including L=0.
Integral_I |g-f|<=Integral_I |g-u|+Integral_I |u-f|<=2*delta*L+epsilon/2<epsilon.
The same g supplies global smoothness, interval bounds, and strict integral error required by T1.
eta=epsilon/2>0; apply T1 at eta to obtain a single globally smooth witness g.
For t in I, 0<g(t)<=C+epsilon/2<=C+epsilon, and Integral_I |g-f|<epsilon/2<epsilon.
f and g are integrable on I, as is |g-f|. This uses the original hypotheses and continuous boundedness of g on I, even if T1's conclusion does not package integrability.
For x,y>=0, (sqrt(x)-sqrt(y))^2<=|x-y|. In case x<=y, subtracting the LHS from y-x gives 2*sqrt(x)*(sqrt(y)-sqrt(x))>=0; the other case is symmetric. Both zero cases are included.
For a.e. t in I, x=2*g(t)>=0 and y=2*f(t)>=0; therefore |sqrt(2*g(t))-sqrt(2*f(t))|^2<=|2*g(t)-2*f(t)|=2*|g(t)-f(t)|.
The squared noise error is measurable under the stated square-root representative convention, using continuity of g, measurability of f, and measurable square root.
The nonnegative squared noise error is integrable on I because it is measurable and dominated a.e. by integrable 2*|g-f|.
Integral_I |sqrt(2*g)-sqrt(2*f)|^2<=2*Integral_I |g-f|.
2*Integral_I |g-f|<2*(epsilon/2)=epsilon. Together with N21 and global smoothness, the same g proves T2.

When a=b, all restricted integrals are zero but g must still be positive and bounded at the singleton. The construction retains delta=epsilon/4>0 and its pointwise bounds, so no degenerate-case exclusion is needed.

error_budgets.strictness: Non-strict is sufficient; delta>0 is needed to request approximation.
Positivity is delta/2>0; no lower bound on f is assumed.
This is the strict slack that makes T1 strict.

boundary_cases.result: All integrals vanish; the interval is a singleton rather than empty, so pointwise g bounds remain required and are met.
f=0 a.e. on I. Clipping gives u=0 everywhere. Strictly positive g and arbitrarily small integrated error coexist; no division by C occurs.
Square-root comparison holds at zero; no Lipschitz constant involving 1/sqrt(f) or positive lower bound on f is used.

boundary_cases.case: f negative or arbitrarily large on an exceptional null set
boundary_cases.result: The coefficient integrals are unchanged and the contraction/noise comparisons hold a.e.; define the square-root integrand using a measurable extension or a.e. representative.
No estimate or integrability outside I is required. The global smooth witness comes from approximation of clipped continuous u, not global integrability of f.
delta scales inversely with L+1; the strict integrated budget remains valid.
All requested smoothing tolerances remain positive.
Only g's smoothness is global. Neither theorem asserts positive lower bounds or upper bounds outside I.

source_gaps_and_obligations.issue: The continuous L1 approximation theorem is invoked without specification. A complete formal proof must supply its hypotheses for restricted Lebesgue measure and ensure q exists on R or can be extended continuously from I.
source_gaps_and_obligations.repair: Use a continuous-function L1 density theorem on the finite interval with ambient functions, or extend an approximant from the compact interval.

source_gaps_and_obligations.issue: Uniform continuity alone does not create a smooth function. The source explicitly invokes a smooth approximation theorem; a full proof must instantiate it to return globally smooth v with the stated compact-set estimate.
source_gaps_and_obligations.repair: Invoke an applicable compact-neighborhood smoothing theorem, or prove it by mollification using uniform continuity on [a-1,b+1].

source_gaps_and_obligations.issue: f may be negative on the exceptional null set, so classical sqrt(2*f(t)) needs an a.e. or extended-real-root convention at those points.
source_gaps_and_obligations.repair: Declare a nonnegative measurable representative or a total measurable real square-root convention. The integral and estimate do not depend on this choice.

source_gaps_and_obligations.issue: The source states that boundedness provides integrability but does not individually construct every measurable/integrable difference and absolute value.
source_gaps_and_obligations.repair: Establish f integrable by a.e. bounded domination; obtain continuous-function integrability on I; close under subtraction and absolute value; derive noise integrability by measurable a.e. domination.

source_gaps_and_obligations.issue: The phrase 'bounded continuous function' could suggest global boundedness of q, while only local boundedness is needed. This does not affect the proof because u is globally bounded after clipping.
source_gaps_and_obligations.repair: If a literal bounded global approximant is required, choose a compactly supported continuous approximant or use an extension followed by clipping.
